cards.German: Als ich am Gate ankam, stiegen die anderen Passagiere bereits ein.
cards.English: When I arrived at the gate, the other passengers [[were already boarding]].
cards.Trap: When I arrived in the Gate, the other passangers already [[stiegen ein]].
cards.Transfer1: When I entered the clinic, the doctor [[was already waiting]].
cards.Rule: Eine Handlung, die in der Vergangenheit gerade im Ablauf war, erfordert Past Continuous (were boarding), und am Gate heißt at the gate.
cards.Alternative1: When I got to the gate, the other passengers were already getting on the plane.

cards.German: Ich wohne seit drei Jahren in Berlin.
cards.English: I [[have been living]] in Berlin [[for]] three years.
cards.Trap: I [[live since]] three years in Berlin.
cards.Transfer1: She [[has been working]] here [[for]] six months.
cards.Rule: Was in der Vergangenheit begann und bis jetzt andauert, steht im Present Perfect (Continuous) – nie im Present Simple. Zeitraum = for, Zeitpunkt = since.
cards.Alternative1: I have lived in Berlin for three years.
cards.Alternative2: I've been living in Berlin for three years.

cards.German: Wenn ich mehr Zeit hätte, würde ich Spanisch lernen.
cards.English: If I [[had]] more time, I [[would learn]] Spanish.
cards.Trap: If I [[would have]] more time, I would learn Spanish.
cards.Transfer1: If she [[knew]] the answer, she [[would tell]] us.
cards.Rule: Im if-Satz des 2. Konditionals steht nie would, sondern das Past Simple. Das would gehört nur in den Hauptsatz.
cards.Alternative1: If I had more time, I'd learn Spanish.

cards.German: Ich freue mich darauf, dich nächste Woche zu sehen.
cards.English: I [[am looking forward to seeing]] you next week.
cards.Trap: I am looking forward [[to see]] you next week.
cards.Transfer1: We [[are looking forward to hearing]] from you.
cards.Rule: Das to in look forward to ist eine Präposition, kein Infinitiv-to – danach folgt deshalb die -ing-Form.
cards.Alternative1: I'm looking forward to seeing you next week.
cards.Alternative2: I look forward to seeing you next week.

cards.German: Er hat mir nicht gesagt, wo der Bahnhof ist.
cards.English: He didn't tell me [[where the station was]].
cards.Trap: He didn't tell me [[where is the station]].
cards.Transfer1: Can you tell me [[what time it is]]?
cards.Rule: In indirekten Fragen gilt die normale Satzstellung (Subjekt vor Verb), ohne do/does/did. Nach einem Einleitungssatz in der Vergangenheit wird die Zeit meist zurückversetzt (is → was).
cards.Alternative1: He didn't tell me where the station is.
cards.Alternative2: He did not tell me where the train station was.
